standard.title: Create fictional situations
standard.description: create and co-create fictional situations based on imagination and/or experience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create arts works that communicate ideas using play, movement, voice and repurposed materials (Foundation). They can draw an idea from imagination or experience and use at least one mode to express it.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and co-create fictional situations — through dramatic play, process drama, puppetry or movement — based on imagination and/or experience.

nodes.label: Accepting and proposing the pretence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can enter a fictional situation created by others and contribute to it — accepting the 'as if' and adding ideas or actions within it.
nodes.minimum_width: Student participates in an established dramatic play scenario, staying in role or accepting the pretence set by a teacher or peer.
nodes.typical_width: Students take turns offering and accepting ideas in improvised drama; they stay in role when participating and suggest relevant roles, situations or props to extend the fictional world.
wider: Students use inquiry questions to propose new situations within the drama ('What else might happen? What if I was there?')
Students co-create a dramatic play space using unstructured materials and everyday clothing items to establish a fictional world
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot accept the pretence — cannot sustain the 'as if' — co-creation collapses into activity rather than drama; creating original fictional situations (the next move) depends on this collaborative foundation.

response_modes.reason: Sustained engagement in the pretence builds through repeated practice in short, clear scenarios; students need regular opportunities to practise entering and extending fictional worlds before they generate original ones.

success_criteria: Student participates in a dramatic play scenario, accepting the fictional situation established by the group
Student contributes at least one idea or action that extends the fictional world

nodes.label: Drawing on imagination and experience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a situation from their own imagination, a story, or personal experience to explore through drama.
nodes.minimum_width: Student names or shows a situation they want to explore — drawn from a story, film, history, fantasy or personal experience.
nodes.typical_width: Students brainstorm and discuss situations from experiences (stories, films, games, personal moments) and use these ideas to initiate improvised drama; they consider what roles and situations might be explored.
wider: Students use puppets they have made from repurposed materials to create new stories that communicate their understanding of existing stories or personal experiences
Students use learning from First Nations Australians' drama that communicates connection to Country/Place to devise drama communicating their own connection to a place in their community

response_modes.reason: Offer varied starting points — familiar stories, personal experiences, fantasy, community events — to help students who struggle to generate ideas from one prompt find a richer entry point.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The breadth of sources available — cultural stories, personal experience, community connections, fantasy — is rich; students who draw on a wider range of starting points develop more expressive range in their drama-making.
success_criteria: Student can name or describe a situation they want to explore in drama, drawing on imagination or experience
Student can explain (however simply) where the idea came from

nodes.label: Creating and co-creating fictional situations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create and co-create fictional situations, using non-verbal and verbal communication to establish role and situation with others.
nodes.minimum_width: Student participates in creating a fictional situation with at least one other person, contributing roles or scenarios and communicating within the drama.
nodes.typical_width: Students contribute ideas and actions within whole-group or small-group improvisations; they communicate non-verbally through facial expressions and movement; they use costume items, props or materials to establish roles and situations; they accept and build on others' contributions.
wider: Students participate in Readers' Theatre, using costume items and props to share information about their character while 'in role'
Students co-create dramatic play with teacher-in-role, responding to the teacher's contributions and extending the fictional world
Students devise short scenes communicating their feelings about a place or how they care for their community, drawing on exploration of First Nations Australians' drama about Country/Place

response_modes.reason: Co-creation integrates the pretence-acceptance and idea-sourcing moves — students must simultaneously contribute, accept, and maintain the fictional world. Teacher scaffolds with process drama strategies and teacher-in-role.

success_criteria: Student creates or co-creates a fictional situation in collaboration with at least one other person
Student uses non-verbal communication (facial expression, movement, gesture) within the drama
Student can describe the role or situation they were exploring
